summary: Agent triage evaluates all 679 Project Agents via LLM without cheap candidate-gen (embeddings exist in intersearch but unused for routing); estimated 85% token reduction available via top-k retrieval
~156 skills × ~8K tokens listed every turn; embedding retrieval could reduce to ~1.3K tokens (80% reduction)
Timestamped OUTPUT_DIR in agent prompts defeats all cross-run prompt cache hits - 0% cache utilization currently
58 plugins share 'inter' prefix — typing /inter narrows to 58 options, not <10 like IDE conventions require
6 distinct 'review' commands across plugins (clavain:review, flux-review, interlore:review, etc.) — user can't tell which to invoke
Tiered skill listing could save ~500 tokens/session — current preamble lists all 232 commands/skills, IDE convention is progressive disclosure (10-15 visible, rest on search)
P1: SessionStart hooks burn 500-800 tok/turn on idle loops even when git SHA and bead state unchanged - session-warm cache pattern from TypeScript watch mode would save 10-16K tok/hour
Salsa manifest pattern exists in gen-skill-compact.sh but not generalized - flux-drive triage could be memoized by (target_hash, roster_hash) saving 2K tok/iterative-review
